entradas.text: Deivid had scheduled a private meeting with me, but he didn't specify what it was about.
"Yes, Deivid. Please come in."
entradas.menu: "Yes, Deivid. Please come in."

entradas.text: "Mr. President. May I come in?"
I heard a knock on the door.
"Take a seat, Mr. Wisci."
entradas.menu: "Take a seat, Mr. Wisci."

entradas.text: "Thank you."
He slowly made his way towards the chair in front of my desk and sat down.
"First of all, thank you for your time."
"Anything for you, Deivid."
entradas.menu: "Anything for you, Deivid."

entradas.text: "Don't mention it. What's wrong?"
entradas.menu: "Don't mention it. What's wrong?"

entradas.text: "Please make it quick. I have other business to attend to."
entradas.menu: "Please make it quick. I have other business to attend to."

entradas.text: "Of course. I will be as fast as I can."
"I wanted to ask you how you are doing."
"It looks like war is truly upon us."
"It must be taking a toll on you, just like it did on me all those years ago."
"But of course, I won't presume to understand what you are going through right now."
"I was never the leader of a nation during wartime, after all."
"I'm fine. Thanks for asking."
entradas.menu: "I'm fine. Thanks for asking."

entradas.text: "I am only interested in the results of this war. Nothing more."
entradas.menu: "I am only interested in the results of this war. Nothing more."

entradas.text: "Honestly. I am tired, Deivid. I am tired of it all."
entradas.menu: "Honestly. I am tired, Deivid. I am tired of it all."

entradas.text: "Please, be sure to take some time for yourself."
"Oh, I know the feeling. Trust me. I know."
"Sometimes you just want to throw away all the responsibility and escape."
"Perhaps into the wilderness, perhaps to the sea."
"That's very good."
"If you ignore the mental fatigue, it will slowly creep in on you. It will poison your thoughts."
"Please be sure to take some time for yourself amid all this."
"If you ignore the mental fatigue, it will slowly creep in on you. It will poison your thoughts."
"I'm not in the mood for lectures."
entradas.menu: "I'm not in the mood for lectures."

entradas.text: "Thank you for your valuable advice."
entradas.menu: "Thank you for your valuable advice."

entradas.text: "Don't mind me. I'm just an old man getting ahead of himself."
"Thank you for taking my advice over the years."
"Don't mind me. I'm just an old man getting ahead of himself."
"Thank you for taking my advice over the years."
"I'm not in the mood for lectures."
entradas.menu: "I'm not in the mood for lectures."

entradas.text: "Thank you for your valuable advice."
entradas.menu: "Thank you for your valuable advice."

entradas.text: "That would be nice, wouldn't it? But I could never do that."
entradas.menu: "That would be nice, wouldn't it? But I could never do that."

entradas.text: "Yes. Exactly. That is what I want to do. I want to get away from this office."
entradas.menu: "Yes. Exactly. That is what I want to do. I want to get away from this office."

entradas.text: "It is good to fantasize, but unfortunately, men of power like yourself are bound by duty and their responsibility to the nation."
"Unfortunately, men of power are bound by duty and their responsibility to the nation."
He started coughing.
"It has been many years since you were in my classroom."
"What a privilege for me."
"I had the chance to watch my student grow into a fine and strong leader in my lifetime. What a privilege indeed."
"You have brought reform to Sordland. You, my student, actually did it."
"You don't know how proud I was to be alongside you."
"You tried your best to bring reform to Sordland. That is valiant in itself."
"It is okay to feel frustrated by failure. But change unfortunately doesn't happen easily."
"You paved a path for future generations to follow, and they will remember you for it."
"If there is one thing I learned from you, it is that power changes people."
"It makes them do things that were not imaginable before."
"I hope you are not trying to take a stab at me right now, Deivid."
entradas.menu: "I hope you are not trying to take a stab at me right now, Deivid."

entradas.text: "It's just a simple observation. Don't pay heed to this old man."
"True. But it changed me for better."
entradas.menu: "True. But it changed me for better."

entradas.text: "Perhaps. But it also takes its toll."
"Desperate times require desperate measures."
entradas.menu: "Desperate times require desperate measures."

entradas.text: "That is correct. But sometimes the ends do not justify the means."
"This was only the beginning. Much more awaits on the horizon."
entradas.menu: "This was only the beginning. Much more awaits on the horizon."

entradas.text: "I still can't believe that we did it."
entradas.menu: "I still can't believe that we did it."

entradas.text: "It wouldn't be possible without you."
entradas.menu: "It wouldn't be possible without you."

entradas.text: "You are too kind, Mr. President."
"You actually managed to make me jump for joy. At my age!"
"I know my student. I know you. You have the capability to do so much more."
"That's the spirit! We can't be sulking about our failures for too long. Otherwise we will spiral into despair."
"That's right. I will do whatever I can to leave a good world for the ones who will come after us."
entradas.menu: "That's right. I will do whatever I can to leave a good world for the ones who will come after us."

entradas.text: "When all is said and done, we still have failed."
entradas.menu: "When all is said and done, we still have failed."

entradas.text: "That is the reality, yes. But, we can't be sulking about our failures for too long. Otherwise we will spiral into despair."
"You are too kind, Mr. President."
"It wouldn't be possible without you."
entradas.menu: "It wouldn't be possible without you."

entradas.text: "This country does not need any more despair."
"So... The elections are fast approaching."
"How are you feeling about your chances?"
Deivid coughed again. This time, for longer.
"We will win. No matter what."
entradas.menu: "We will win. No matter what."

entradas.text: "I can't say for sure, but I'm hopeful."
entradas.menu: "I can't say for sure, but I'm hopeful."

entradas.text: "We will see."
entradas.menu: "We will see."

entradas.text: "Good. That is what a leader should say."
"Uncertainty doesn't suit you, Mr. President."
"I'm afraid I have an announcement to make to you."
"Go on."
entradas.menu: "Go on."

entradas.text: "Why? What's wrong?"
entradas.menu: "Why? What's wrong?"

entradas.text: "An announcement? What kind?"
entradas.menu: "An announcement? What kind?"

entradas.text: "After the term is done, I will be retiring."
"I would be lying if I said I wasn't expecting this."
entradas.menu: "I would be lying if I said I wasn't expecting this."

entradas.text: "For what reason?"
entradas.menu: "For what reason?"

entradas.text: "Deivid. I can't accept this. You're irreplaceable in my cabinet."
entradas.menu: "Deivid. I can't accept this. You're irreplaceable in my cabinet."

entradas.text: "I have been in this line of work for many decades now."
"I swore an oath to myself years ago."
"I would quit if I ever felt like I didn't have the physical capability to serve anymore. At that point, I would become a hindrance."
"That time has come, Mr. President."
"My bones are aching, my hands are shaking, my voice is failing."
"Besides, I am sure you can find a younger minister who is a little more full of life."
He winked at me and chuckled which turned into another cough.
"I see. Thank you for letting me know."
entradas.menu: "I see. Thank you for letting me know."

entradas.text: "You have been a mentor, a teacher and a friend. Thank you for your service to this country."
entradas.menu: "You have been a mentor, a teacher and a friend. Thank you for your service to this country."

entradas.text: "You will be sorely missed, Deivid."
entradas.menu: "You will be sorely missed, Deivid."

entradas.text: "It was an honor, Mr. President."
Deivid stood up to leave.
We shook hands.
entradas.menu: Shake his hand.

entradas.text: We hugged.
entradas.menu: Hug Deivid.

entradas.text: "Best of luck, Anton."
"Thank you."
He turned around and left.
"Before I go, I want to mention something."
He looked around before grabbing my arm and lowering his voice.
"Be careful of the military. I think they are planning something."
"I have lived long enough to see two coups in my lifetime, and let's just say I have gotten better at recognizing the signs."
"You must remember what happened to my father Anton. Just be careful and take care of your family."
"Take this as the last piece of advice from me."
He suddenly raised his voice again.
"We are probably being watched so I must be very brief."
"I overheard a conversation the other day near a newspaper stand."
"I overheard a conversation the other day near a newspaper stand."
"I overheard a conversation the other day near a newspaper stand."
"I overheard a conversation the other day near a newspaper stand."
"They were calling you a die-hard Malenyevist."
"What do you think about that?"
"It piqued my interest so I kept listening. They were talking about you."
"It piqued my interest so I kept listening. They were talking about you."
"They were calling you a die-hard Sollist."
"What do you think about that?"
"It piqued my interest so I kept listening. They were talking about you."
"They were calling you a die hard capitalist."
"What do you think about that?"
"It piqued my interest so I kept listening. They were talking about you."
"They were calling you a die hard democrat."
"What do you think about that?"
"I refuse to be called a Malenyevist."
entradas.menu: "I refuse to be called a Malenyevist."

entradas.text: "They weren't wrong. I *am* a die-hard Malenyevist."
entradas.menu: "They weren't wrong. I *am* a die-hard Malenyevist."

entradas.text: "They weren't wrong. I *am* a die-hard Sollist."
entradas.menu: "They weren't wrong. I *am* a die-hard Sollist."

entradas.text: "I refuse to be called a Sollist."
entradas.menu: "I refuse to be called a Sollist."

entradas.text: "They weren't wrong. I *am* a die-hard capitalist."
entradas.menu: "They weren't wrong. I *am* a die-hard capitalist."

entradas.text: "I refuse to be called a capitalist."
entradas.menu: "I refuse to be called a capitalist."

entradas.text: "They weren't wrong. I *am* a die hard democrat."
entradas.menu: "They weren't wrong. I *am* a die-hard democrat."

entradas.text: "I refuse to be called a democrat."
entradas.menu: "I refuse to be called a democrat."

entradas.text: "My father, Artor S. Wisci, used to say, 'Always know yourself'."

"What do you think about that?"
"I refuse that statement. I don't think I am an authoritarian."

He stopped for a moment and took a quick look at his watch.
"It's at least good to know that you do."
"I respect your honesty."
"Mr. President. May I come in?"
